title: Launch day breathe sheet & operator cheatbag
content:
Purpose:
This is a compact, operator-focused "breathe sheet" for launch day: a single-page mental model + actionable checklist to keep the team breathing during the cutover. Not comprehensive — use alongside the full runbook (Confluence link above).

Status: draft — intended for on-call and shift leads. Last updated by Maya 2026-11-08.

High-level rollout window (UTC):
- 08:00–09:00: preflight and dry smoke (staging-like traffic)
- 09:00–10:00: soft canary 5% (region: us-west1)
- 10:00–11:30: ramp to 20% if healthy
- 11:30–12:30: gradual global rollout to 100% (staged regions)

Who to page (priority):
- SRE lead: Jamal Rivers (page, call if infra CPU > 85% sustained 5m)
- Serving-runtime lead: Sofia Alvarez (call if token latency p95 > 800ms)
- Product owner: Priya Nandakumar (business impact decision)
- Escalation CTO on-call: Eli Novak (critical incidents only)

Preflight quick checklist (T minus 60 -> 0):
- [ ] Confirm canary image hash (platform PR #981) matches release tag
- [ ] Verify infra quota: GPUs available in target regions (infra dashboard)
- [ ] Load test smoke: synthetic qps to canary endpoints (commands below)
- [ ] Confirm alerting runbook links are pinned to release channel
- [ ] Confirm telemetry dashboards loaded: token-cost, latency-by-route, model-variants
- [ ] Confirm roll-forward and rollback artifacts exist in S3 (s3://releases/2026-11/)

Operator quick commands (copy-paste in terminal):
- Trigger canary deployment: kubectl apply -f k8s/canary-deploy.yaml --context=prod-us-west1
- Force traffic split to canary (traffic service): curl -X POST $TRAFFIC_API/set?split=canary:5%
- Restart worker if mem spike: kubectl rollout restart deploy/worker-x --namespace=production
- Abort rollout (fast rollback): curl -X POST $TRAFFIC_API/set?split=primary:100% && kubectl set image deploy/frontend frontend=frontend:previous

Smoke tests (fast, must pass before any traffic increase):
- Auth + tokenexchange (10 requests, 200 OK >= 9/10)
- Small-generation load (50 short prompts, p95 latency < 350ms)
- Embeddings check (sample 20 vectors, L2 sanity)
- KV cache warm check (hit ratio > 70% for short prompts)

Telemetry anchors & thresholds (auto-escalate if hit):
- Token generation p95 > 900ms for 3 consecutive samples -> page Sofia
- Error rate (5xx) > 0.5% sustained 10m -> page Jamal + shift lead
- Token cost per 1k tokens spike +20% vs baseline -> investigate model variant routing
- Request queue depth > 300 -> activate backpressure lane and throttle new sessions

Canary rules (explicit):
- If any smoke test fails -> immediate rollback to previous image
- If p95 latency increases by > 30% vs baseline -> pause ramp and A/B compare telemetry
- If error spike is transient (<2 min) and no user-facing errors -> observe; if >5 min -> rollback

Release notes (draft — publish to docs after go):
- Feature: rollout of adaptive-batching v2 (reduces per-token cost in short-prompt workloads)
- Performance: average token cost down ~8% on baseline conversational tests
- Ops: new traffic-splitting API with time-bounded splits and auto-fallback
- Known limitations: small fraction of long-seq requests may see transient p99 increases; rolling mitigations in-progress

Post-release checklist (T+0 -> T+72h):
- [ ] Sampling: collect golden set prompts and run regression tests nightly for 72h
- [ ] Billing check: reconcile token billing for first 24h window
- [ ] Telemetry: snapshot dashboards and tag them with release id
- [ ] Customer-notices: coordinate with CS for any unexpected churn
- [ ] Retrospective: add one-liner notes while fresh to this doc; schedule 48h postmortem if any P1/P0

Quick forensics template (when an alert fires):
- Time window, affected regions, perturbed service(s)
- Traffic percentage on canary vs primary
- Recent infra events (restarts, autoscaler activity, node replacements)
- Commanded operator actions and timestamps
- Attach telemetry links (span traces, logs, error rates)

Notes to self / open questions (raw):
- Need a short-circuit for embeddings-only customers to keep stable during mixed-rollouts? explore traffic-tagging
- Should we add an automated rollback if cost/latency delta triggers within 15m? (ops risk vs noise)
- Check with infra about scheduled node maintenance windows in europe-west1 (I saw alarm for maintenance on 2026-11-09)

Retrospective prompts (fill in T+48h):
- What was the single biggest surprise?
- Which alert was noisy / which was signal-first?
- Did operator quick commands behave as expected?
- One sentence to improve for next launch (ops + infra + product)

Appendix: quick links
- Full release plan: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/REL/Release+Plan+2026-11
- Rollout PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/platform/pull/981
- Incident channel: https://slack.redwood.ai/archives/CRELEASEDAY
- Canary control API: https://internal-api.redwood.ai/traffic-control

End (keep this doc small and updated — copy into the shift binder before your watch).

-- Maya
